match.reason: No existing point covers judging a business on financial, social and environmental results together: profit and business-in-the-economy are related but narrower ideas.

draft.title: Management and the triple bottom line
card: The triple bottom line judges a business on three kinds of result, not on profit alone. The three are financial, social and environmental.
Financial
profit, sales and returns to owners. This is the result a business has always measured.
Social
the effect on people, such as employees, customers and the community. Examples are safe work, fair pay and local support.
Environmental
the effect on nature, such as the energy used, the waste made and the pollution released. Managers who use this approach report on all three areas.
draft.remember: The triple bottom line asks how a business did on money, people and the environment.

a.q: Which statement best describes the triple bottom line?
opts: Judging a business on money, people and the environment
Judging a business on profit, sales and customer numbers
Judging a business on its owners, staff and customers
Judging a business on how well it follows the law
a.why: The triple bottom line has three parts: financial, social and environmental results. The option about profit, sales and customer numbers is tempting, but all three are financial measures, so it leaves out the social and environmental results.
a.clue: Think of the three areas named in the card.

b.q: Priya manages a furniture maker in Newcastle. Her yearly report covers profit, staff safety records and the amount of timber waste sent to landfill. What does the report show?
opts: It reports on all three parts of the triple bottom line
It reports on the financial part only
It reports on the financial and social parts only
It reports on the social and environmental parts only
b.why: Profit is a financial result, staff safety is a social result and timber waste is an environmental result. The report covers all three. A student might miss the waste figure and choose the financial and social option, but waste is about the effect on the environment.
b.clue: Sort each item in the report into money, people or environment.

a.best: Judging a business on money, people and the environment

b.best: It reports on all three parts of the triple bottom line

problems.detail: The why calls customer numbers a financial measure. A customer count is not money, and the card lists customers under the social result, so this could confuse students. It would be clearer to say the option covers only business or sales results and leaves out social and environmental effects.
